meta.title: Web Cache Poisoning & Unkeyed Header Reflection (X-Forwarded-Host / X-Original-URL)
meta.plainExplanation: Probes an isolated cache-busted URL (?secscan_cb=<nonce>) with unkeyed forwarding headers (X-Forwarded-Host, X-Host, X-Original-URL) and performs a clean follow-up request to verify whether the reflected header is stored in a shared HTTP cache.
meta.whyItMatters: If a reverse proxy or CDN caches a response containing an unkeyed header value, an attacker can poison the shared cache and serve malicious scripts or redirects to all visitors.
meta.defaultFix: Include X-Forwarded-Host / X-Forwarded-Scheme in the cache key (Vary header), or configure the web server and framework to ignore unauthenticated X-Forwarded-Host and X-Original-URL headers.
meta.remediation: Include X-Forwarded-Host / X-Forwarded-Scheme in the cache key (Vary header), or configure the web server and framework to ignore unauthenticated X-Forwarded-Host and X-Original-URL headers.

meta.plainExplanation: Inspects client-side JavaScript in HTML responses for direct untrusted DOM source-to-sink dataflows (location.hash / location.search flowing into innerHTML / document.write / eval) and window.addEventListener("message") handlers lacking event.origin validation.

findings.detail: No SSRF backend URL-fetcher surface detected.

meta.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) URL Parameter & Backend Fetcher Surface
meta.plainExplanation: Tests URL/webhook/callback query parameters (?url=, ?webhook=, ?uri=) with a non-routable RFC 2606 domain (http://secscan-ssrf-probe.invalid/) to detect whether the backend server attempts an outbound HTTP fetch and leaks HTTP client connection errors.
meta.whyItMatters: Unvalidated server-side URL fetchers allow attackers to pivot into internal VPC networks, query cloud instance metadata services (169.254.169.254), and scan internal ports.
meta.defaultFix: Validate user-supplied URLs against a strict domain allowlist, connect directly to the validated IP (PinnedDialer), and block all RFC1918, loopback, link-local, and cloud metadata IP ranges.
meta.remediation: Validate user-supplied URLs against a strict domain allowlist, connect directly to the validated IP (PinnedDialer), and block all RFC1918, loopback, link-local, and cloud metadata IP ranges.

meta.title: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI — Jinja2, Twig, Freemarker, EL, ERB, EJS)
meta.plainExplanation: Tests URL query parameters with non-destructive arithmetic template expressions across Jinja2/Twig/Pebble ({{7919*13}}), Freemarker/Spring EL/Thymeleaf (${7919*13}), and ERB/EJS (<%= 7919*13 %>), verifying that the server evaluates the expression to 102947 without reflecting the un-evaluated formula.
meta.whyItMatters: When user input is concatenated directly into a server-side template string before rendering, attackers can execute arbitrary template expressions and achieve remote code execution (RCE).
meta.defaultFix: Never pass user-supplied strings as template source code. Always pass user data as named context variables into pre-compiled static templates.
meta.remediation: Never pass user-supplied strings as template source code. Always pass user data as named context variables into pre-compiled static templates.

meta.plainExplanation: Scans for exposed operational telemetry (/metrics, /prometheus, /server-status, /actuator/health), server 5xx errors, slow response latency, uncompressed payloads, and expiring TLS certificates.
meta.whyItMatters: Publicly accessible operational metrics, server status, and detailed component health dumps reveal internal architectures, infrastructure utilization, and sensitive service names to unauthorized actors.
meta.defaultFix: Restrict operational and telemetry endpoints to authorized monitoring networks or require authentication. Enable gzip/brotli compression, resolve backend server errors, and renew SSL/TLS certificates before expiration.

meta.title: XML External Entity (XXE) & Unsafe XML/SOAP Entity Expansion
meta.plainExplanation: Safely tests XML-accepting endpoints with a benign internal DTD entity declaration (<!ENTITY secscanxxe "secscan_xxe_eval_9412">) to verify whether custom DOCTYPE entities are expanded or whether raw XML parser exceptions are disclosed.
meta.whyItMatters: XML parsers that permit DOCTYPE declarations and entity resolution allow attackers to read arbitrary local files, probe internal networks via SSRF, or trigger denial-of-service.
meta.defaultFix: Disable DOCTYPE declarations (disallow-doctype-decl = true) and external entities in your XML parser.
meta.remediation: Disable DOCTYPE declarations (disallow-doctype-decl = true) and external entities in your XML parser.
